tutorial.audience: GMs create, reveal, resolve, import, and export targets and grant/recharge scanners. Players may scan from owned tokens when world settings allow it and, by default, only when that Actor has a grant. The HoloSuite tile is player-visible.

quickStart.title: Create and detect a target
steps: On the active Scene, draw a Region around the hidden passage, object, or area.
Open Pulse Scanner as GM, stay on Targets, and choose New Target.
Link the Region, choose a signal and type, set Reticle/Icon/Region ping, visibility, status, color, integrity when relevant, and description, then save.
Open Scanners, select the player’s Actor, choose scanner name, signal, range in scene units, and charges, then Grant Scanner.
As the player, control an owned token, open Pulse Scanner, select the grant, and scan inside range.
Use the manager to Reveal, Hide, Resolve, or recharge the scanner as the investigation changes.

sections.title: Target configuration

rows: Signature name; defaults from the selected type.
Required practical anchor. Its bounds supply target center/radius and Region-outline geometry.
Signal that can detect the target.
Semantic icon/color and, for Breakable, integrity behavior.
Reticle, type Icon, or exact Region outline.
0–100, shown for Breakable targets when enabled.
Eleven supplied colors plus preserved valid custom hex values.

paragraphs: Target records also normalize a numeric difficulty, icon, center, and radius for API/import compatibility. Region geometry is reapplied at scan time, so moving/resizing the linked Region updates the effective scan point.

sections.title: Signals and target types

rows: Magic Residue, Tech Signature, Biological Trace

paragraphs: The manager can explicitly pair any target with a scanner mode. Type-to-mode lists supply sensible defaults rather than a permanent restriction.

sections.title: Granting scanners and charges

rows: Actor that receives the scanner flag.
Display name; default comes from the world setting.
One of the six modes used by player scans.
Range in the active Scene’s distance units, converted to pixels from grid settings.
Remaining uses; cannot exceed Max after normalization.

bullets: An Actor can hold multiple named scanner grants.
Each limited scan consumes one charge before scanning. A player may reduce their own charge through normal use but cannot recharge or edit grant configuration.
Use Save in the scanner overview to change Max and Now; Remove revokes one grant.
The API can revoke all grants by omitting a scanner ID.
For performance, keep ordinary scanner ranges at 100 scene units or less.

sections.title: How a scan is resolved
steps: The module resolves the selected token, falling back to the user’s character token or another owned token with scanner access.
For players it verifies Allow Players to Scan, token ownership, and the required Actor grant. GMs can scan without those player restrictions.
The token center becomes the origin. Grant radius is converted from scene units; each target’s linked Region supplies its effective location/size.
Targets must be in range and match the selected mode. GMs may additionally supply type/mode filters through the API.
The module plays the pulse sound, temporarily locks canvas pan/drag/wheel during the effect, and renders up to its safe target limit.
The latest target IDs are retained locally so a GM can Reveal Latest Scan.
paragraphs: A player scan returns sanitized target objects. GM visibility strips sensitive description/difficulty details from the player payload until state is revealed; do not treat Scene flags as secure secret storage against users inspecting client data.

sections.title: Pulse, pings, labels, and sound
bullets: The pulse color follows the scanner signal and expands from the token center.
Reticle uses a circular marker sized from target radius; Icon uses the type icon; Region draws polygon/circle/ellipse outlines from Foundry Region geometry.
No matching targets displays NO SIGNATURES DETECTED.
Default Highlight Duration controls the visible result lifetime; internal normalization keeps unsafe extremes bounded.
Show Labels To Players controls result labels. Show Integrity To Players controls Breakable integrity bars.
Scan Pulse Sound can use the bundled MP3, a custom uploaded audio path, or no sound.

rows: Not included in ordinary non-GM getTargets results; scan payload sanitization applies when detected.
Player-visible persistent target state intended to remain available.
Sets visibility/status to Revealed, unless already Resolved.
Reveals every target found by the GM’s latest scan on the current Scene.
Returns visibility to GM and status to Active.
Marks Resolved and Revealed, useful for destroyed walls or collected evidence.
Returns to Active and GM visibility.

sections.title: Import, export, and storage
paragraphs: Targets are stored as a hidden flag on their Scene. Export produces JSON with module/version, source Scene metadata, timestamp, and targets. Import can merge into or replace the current Scene’s target store; colliding IDs are regenerated and every target is rebound to the destination Scene.

callouts.title: Regions are references
callouts.text: Imported targets retain Region IDs but do not create Regions. Re-link targets when the destination Scene uses different Region document IDs.

sections.title: Public API and scan-complete hook
paragraphs: Use game.pulseScanner or the module api property.

rows: createTarget, getTargets, deleteTarget, revealTarget, revealLatestScan, hideTarget, resolveTarget, unresolveTarget

paragraphs: scanCompleteHook is the string pulse-scanner.scanComplete. After an allowed scan, the initiating client calls that local hook with sceneId, userId, and anonymous x/y points only—no target IDs, labels, descriptions, Actors, or Tokens. Empty successful scans include an empty points array; denied scans do not fire. Consumers must enforce permissions and coarsen locations before sharing them.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
bullets: No target found: confirm range, Region placement, target mode, scanner signal, active status, and current Scene.
Player cannot scan: enable Allow Players to Scan, control an owned token, and grant that Actor a scanner when Require Pulse Scanner Access is on.
No charges: recharge Current Charges as GM or set Max Charges to 0 for unlimited use.
Region outline is wrong: check the Region’s supported shapes and reopen after editing; the module falls back to bounds if exact geometry is unavailable.
Labels/integrity missing for players: enable their world display settings and ensure visibility/sanitization permits the data.
Custom sound is silent: select Custom uploaded sound and provide a readable audio path.
Imported target points nowhere: recreate/relink the destination Scene Region.

reference.title: Complete settings reference

rows: Require a scanner grant for non-GMs.
Target label display in player result effects.
Path used only in Custom mode.
Default maximum for new grants; 0 unlimited.

paragraphs: Default scanner signal (Structural) and default grant radius (30 scene units) are hidden settings managed through the Scanners workflow.

faq.question: Do players need an inventory Item to scan?
faq.answer: No. This release uses Actor-based scanner grants, not a world Item workflow.

faq.question: What does Max Charges 0 mean?
faq.answer: Unlimited scans. Positive maxima consume one Current Charge per use.

faq.question: Why does an imported target not follow its Region?
faq.answer: Region IDs are references and may differ between Scenes/worlds. Edit the target and link a Region in the destination Scene.

faq.question: Can a player recharge their scanner?
faq.answer: No. Players can consume charges through scanning; only a GM can increase/reconfigure them.

faq.question: Does the scanComplete hook reveal targets?
faq.answer: No. It is local and contains only Scene/user IDs and x/y points. It grants no access and sends no target identity or metadata.
